message.content:
Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-rays demonstrate marked tracheobronchomegaly (dilated trachea and main bronchi) and extensive cystic bronchiectasis with multiple large cavities, which are hallmark features of Mounier-Kuhn syndrome. The progression to increased number and size of these cavities indicates worsening disease, requiring management focused on airway clearance (physiotherapy) and treatment of superimposed infections with antibiotics.
